import fs from "fs";
import os from "os";
import path from "path";

const H = os.homedir();
const SRC = path.join(H, "dev", "toxicwind", "vansrouter-omp");
const EXT = path.join(SRC, "extensions");
const NOW = new Date().toISOString().replace(/[:.]/g, "-").slice(0, 19);

function say(t) { console.log(""); console.log("== " + t + " =="); }
function run(cmd, cwd) {
  const p = Bun.spawnSync(["bash", "-lc", cmd], { cwd: cwd || H, stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" });
  return { code: p.exitCode, out: p.stdout.toString().trim(), err: p.stderr.toString().trim() };
}

say("0 verify fork checkout");
if (!fs.existsSync(SRC)) {
  console.error("missing " + SRC);
  console.error("clone first: git clone https://github.com/QMahyar/pi-9router.git vansrouter-omp");
  process.exit(1);
}
fs.mkdirSync(EXT, { recursive: true });

const TARGET = path.join(EXT, "vansrouter.ts");
const BAK1 = path.join(EXT, "vansrouter.ts.bak1");
const BAK2 = path.join(EXT, "vansrouter.ts.bak2");

say("1 rotate existing backups");

try { fs.copyFileSync(BAK1, BAK2); } catch {}

say("2 write extension");

const EXTENSION_SOURCE = [
  '// extensions/vansrouter.ts',
  '// OMP-native VansRouter provider extension.',
  '//',
  '// Multi-tier:',
  '//   Discovery:  dynamic /v1/models -> disk cache (3 rotations) -> seed list',
  '//   Health:     /api/health -> /v1/models -> TCP connect -> unregistered',
  '//   Resilience: /api/breaker + /api/quota/kimchi + /api/proxies -> status only',
  '//   ACL:        /api/key/info -> unfiltered on failure',
  '//   Write:      rotate main -> bak1 -> bak2, then atomic rename',
  '//',
  '// Uses pi.registerProvider + fetchDynamicModels + ctx.ui.* only.',
  '// No createProvider (#9024). No @earendil-works/* or @mariozechner/* (#6470/#7174/#6333).',
  '',
  'import type { ExtensionAPI } from "@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent";',
  'import { promises as fsp } from "node:fs";',
  'import path from "node:path";',
  'import os from "node:os";',
  'import net from "node:net";',
  '',
  'const VR_BASE = process.env.VANSROUTER_URL ?? process.env.NINEROUTER_URL ?? "http://127.0.0.1:20128";',
  'const VR_KEY_ENV = "VANSROUTER_API_KEY";',
  'const VR_KEY_FALLBACK_ENV = "NINEROUTER_KEY";',
  '',
  'const CACHE_DIR = path.join(os.homedir(), ".omp", "agent", "cache");',
  'const CATALOG_MAIN = path.join(CACHE_DIR, "vansrouter-catalog.json");',
  'const CATALOG_BAK1 = path.join(CACHE_DIR, "vansrouter-catalog.bak1.json");',
  'const CATALOG_BAK2 = path.join(CACHE_DIR, "vansrouter-catalog.bak2.json");',
  'const RESILIENCE_CACHE = path.join(CACHE_DIR, "vansrouter-resilience.json");',
  '',
  'const HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS = 3000;',
  'const HEALTH_TIMEOUT_MS = 1500;',
  'const DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT_MS = 8000;',
  '',
  'const SEED_MODELS = [',
  '  { id: "oc/jev-1.13-free", name: "OpenCode Jev Free", contextWindow: 128000, maxTokens: 8192 },',
  '  { id: "oc/mimo-v2.5-free", name: "OpenCode Mimo Free", contextWindow: 128000, maxTokens: 8192 },',
  '  { id: "oc/nemotron-3.5-lightning-free", name: "OpenCode Nemotron Lightning Free", contextWindow: 128000, maxTokens: 8192 },',
  '  { id: "oc/deepseek-v4-flash-free", name: "OpenCode DeepSeek Flash Free", contextWindow: 128000, maxTokens: 8192 },',
  '  { id: "mmf/mimo-auto", name: "MMF Mimo Auto", contextWindow: 128000, maxTokens: 8192 },',
  '];',
  '',
  'interface ModelEntry { id: string; name: string; contextWindow: number; maxTokens: number; }',
  'interface Catalog { fetchedAt: number; source: "dynamic" | "cache-main" | "cache-bak1" | "cache-bak2" | "seed"; models: ModelEntry[]; }',
  'interface ResilienceStatus {',
  '  fetchedAt: number;',
  '  breaker: { open?: number } | null;',
  '  quota: { daysUntilReset?: number } | null;',
  '  proxies: { dead?: number; pools?: number } | null;',
  '  acl: { allowedProviders?: string[]; allowedKinds?: string[] } | null;',
  '}',
  '',
  'async function httpJson<T>(url: string, init: RequestInit = {}, timeoutMs = HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS): Promise<T | null> {',
  '  try {',
  '    const res = await fetch(url, { ...init, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs) });',
  '    if (!res.ok) return null;',
  '    return (await res.json()) as T;',
  '  } catch { return null; }',
  '}',
  '',
  'function authHeaders(key: string): Record<string, string> {',
  '  return key ? { Authorization: "Bearer " + key } : {};',
  '}',
  '',
  'async function probeHealth(base: string): Promise<boolean> {',
  '  const h = await httpJson<{ ok?: boolean }>(base + "/api/health", {}, HEALTH_TIMEOUT_MS);',
  '  if (h && h.ok !== false) return true;',
  '  const m = await httpJson<unknown>(base + "/v1/models", {}, HEALTH_TIMEOUT_MS);',
  '  if (m) return true;',
  '  return tcpProbe(base);',
  '}',
  '',
  'function tcpProbe(base: string): Promise<boolean> {',
  '  return new Promise((resolve) => {',
  '    try {',
  '      const u = new URL(base);',
  '      const port = Number(u.port || (u.protocol === "https:" ? 443 : 80));',
  '      const sock = net.connect({ host: u.hostname, port }, () => { sock.destroy(); resolve(true); });',
  '      sock.on("error", () => { sock.destroy(); resolve(false); });',
  '      sock.setTimeout(1500, () => { sock.destroy(); resolve(false); });',
  '    } catch { resolve(false); }',
  '  });',
  '}',
  '',
  'async function fetchCatalogDynamic(base: string, key: string): Promise<ModelEntry[] | null> {',
  '  const body = await httpJson<{ data?: Array<Record<string, unknown>> }>(base + "/v1/models", { headers: authHeaders(key) }, DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT_MS);',
  '  if (!body?.data || !Array.isArray(body.data)) return null;',
  '  const seen = new Set<string>();',
  '  const out: ModelEntry[] = [];',
  '  for (const raw of body.data) {',
  '    const id = typeof raw.id === "string" ? raw.id : null;',
  '    if (!id || seen.has(id)) continue;',
  '    seen.add(id);',
  '    out.push({',
  '      id,',
  '      name: typeof raw.name === "string" ? raw.name : id,',
  '      contextWindow: typeof raw.context_window === "number" ? raw.context_window : typeof raw.contextWindow === "number" ? raw.contextWindow : 128000,',
  '      maxTokens: typeof raw.max_tokens === "number" ? raw.max_tokens : typeof raw.maxTokens === "number" ? raw.maxTokens : 8192,',
  '    });',
  '  }',
  '  return out.length ? out : null;',
  '}',
  '',
  'async function readCatalogFromDisk(): Promise<Catalog | null> {',
  '  const files: Array<[string, Catalog["source"]]> = [[CATALOG_MAIN, "cache-main"], [CATALOG_BAK1, "cache-bak1"], [CATALOG_BAK2, "cache-bak2"]];',
  '  for (const [f, src] of files) {',
  '    try {',
  '      const parsed = JSON.parse(await fsp.readFile(f, "utf8")) as Partial<Catalog>;',
  '      if (Array.isArray(parsed.models) && parsed.models.length > 0) {',
  '        return { fetchedAt: typeof parsed.fetchedAt === "number" ? parsed.fetchedAt : 0, source: src, models: parsed.models as ModelEntry[] };',
  '      }',
  '    } catch {}',
  '  }',
  '  return null;',
  '}',
  '',
  'async function writeCatalogWithBackup(catalog: Catalog): Promise<void> {',
  '  await fsp.mkdir(CACHE_DIR, { recursive: true });',
  '  try { await fsp.copyFile(CATALOG_MAIN, CATALOG_BAK1); } catch {}',
  '  try { await fsp.copyFile(CATALOG_BAK1, CATALOG_BAK2); } catch {}',
  '  const tmp = CATALOG_MAIN + ".tmp";',
  '  await fsp.writeFile(tmp, JSON.stringify(catalog, null, 2), { mode: 0o600 });',
  '  await fsp.rename(tmp, CATALOG_MAIN);',
  '}',
  '',
  'async function resolveCatalog(base: string, key: string): Promise<Catalog> {',
  '  const dyn = await fetchCatalogDynamic(base, key);',
  '  if (dyn) {',
  '    const c: Catalog = { fetchedAt: Date.now(), source: "dynamic", models: dyn };',
  '    await writeCatalogWithBackup(c);',
  '    return c;',
  '  }',
  '  const cached = await readCatalogFromDisk();',
  '  if (cached) return cached;',
  '  return { fetchedAt: Date.now(), source: "seed", models: SEED_MODELS };',
  '}',
  '',
  'async function probeResilience(base: string, key: string): Promise<ResilienceStatus> {',
  '  const h = authHeaders(key);',
  '  const [b, q, p, a] = await Promise.allSettled([',
  '    httpJson<ResilienceStatus["breaker"]>(base + "/api/breaker", { headers: h }),',
  '    httpJson<ResilienceStatus["quota"]>(base + "/api/quota/kimchi", { headers: h }),',
  '    httpJson<ResilienceStatus["proxies"]>(base + "/api/proxies", { headers: h }),',
  '    httpJson<ResilienceStatus["acl"]>(base + "/api/key/info", { headers: h }),',
  '  ]);',
  '  const pick = <T>(r: PromiseSettledResult<T | null>): T | null => r.status === "fulfilled" ? r.value : null;',
  '  const status: ResilienceStatus = { fetchedAt: Date.now(), breaker: pick(b), quota: pick(q), proxies: pick(p), acl: pick(a) };',
  '  try {',
  '    await fsp.mkdir(CACHE_DIR, { recursive: true });',
  '    await fsp.writeFile(RESILIENCE_CACHE, JSON.stringify(status, null, 2), { mode: 0o600 });',
  '  } catch {}',
  '  return status;',
  '}',
  '',
  'function applyAclFilter(models: ModelEntry[], acl: ResilienceStatus["acl"]): ModelEntry[] {',
  '  if (!acl) return models;',
  '  const { allowedProviders } = acl;',
  '  if (!allowedProviders) return models;',
  '  return models.filter((m) => allowedProviders.includes(m.id.split("/")[0]));',
  '}',
  '',
  'function formatStatusLine(catalog: Catalog, status: ResilienceStatus | null): string {',
  '  const parts: string[] = [];',
  '  const tag = catalog.source === "dynamic" ? "" : catalog.source.startsWith("cache") ? " (" + catalog.source.replace("cache-", "") + ")" : " (seed)";',
  '  parts.push("VR:" + catalog.models.length + tag);',
  '  if (status?.breaker?.open) parts.push(status.breaker.open + " tripped");',
  '  if (status?.quota?.daysUntilReset) parts.push(status.quota.daysUntilReset + "d reset");',
  '  if (status?.proxies?.dead) parts.push(status.proxies.dead + " dead");',
  '  return parts.join(" - ");',
  '}',
  '',
  'export default function vansrouterExtension(pi: ExtensionAPI) {',
  '  let lastCatalog: Catalog | null = null;',
  '  let lastStatus: ResilienceStatus | null = null;',
  '',
  '  function resolveKey(): string {',
  '    return process.env[VR_KEY_ENV] ?? process.env[VR_KEY_FALLBACK_ENV] ?? "";',
  '  }',
  '',
  '  async function syncAndRegister(ctx: any, reason: string): Promise<void> {',
  '    const healthy = await probeHealth(VR_BASE);',
  '    if (!healthy) {',
  '      ctx.ui?.notify?.("VansRouter unreachable at " + VR_BASE + " (" + reason + ")", "warn");',
  '      return;',
  '    }',
  '    const catalog = await resolveCatalog(VR_BASE, resolveKey());',
  '    lastCatalog = catalog;',
  '    const status = await probeResilience(VR_BASE, resolveKey());',
  '    lastStatus = status;',
  '    const filtered = applyAclFilter(catalog.models, status.acl);',
  '    const visible = filtered.length ? filtered : catalog.models;',
  '    pi.registerProvider("vansrouter", {',
  '      baseUrl: VR_BASE + "/v1",',
  '      apiKey: VR_KEY_ENV,',
  '      api: "openai-completions",',
  '      authHeader: true,',
  '      fetchDynamicModels: async (apiKey: string) => {',
  '        const dyn = await fetchCatalogDynamic(VR_BASE, apiKey);',
  '        if (dyn) {',
  '          const fd = applyAclFilter(dyn, lastStatus?.acl ?? null);',
  '          const vis = fd.length ? fd : dyn;',
  '          lastCatalog = { fetchedAt: Date.now(), source: "dynamic", models: vis };',
  '          await writeCatalogWithBackup(lastCatalog);',
  '          return vis;',
  '        }',
  '        return visible;',
  '      },',
  '    });',
  '    try { ctx.ui?.setStatus?.("vansrouter", formatStatusLine(catalog, status)); } catch {}',
  '  }',
  '',
  '  pi.on("session_start", async (_e: unknown, ctx: any) => { await syncAndRegister(ctx, "session_start"); });',
  '',
  '  pi.registerCommand?.("vansrouter", {',
  '    description: "VansRouter provider control",',
  '    handler: async (args: string, ctx: any) => {',
  '      const sub = (args || "").trim().split(/\\s+/)[0] || "status";',
  '      if (sub === "status") {',
  '        const cat = lastCatalog ?? (await readCatalogFromDisk()) ?? { fetchedAt: 0, source: "seed" as const, models: SEED_MODELS };',
  '        ctx.ui?.notify?.(formatStatusLine(cat, lastStatus) + "\\nbase: " + VR_BASE + "\\nkey: " + (resolveKey() ? "present" : "MISSING") + "\\nmodels: " + cat.models.map((m) => m.id).join(", "), "info");',
  '        return;',
  '      }',
  '      if (sub === "sync") { await syncAndRegister(ctx, "manual sync"); ctx.ui?.notify?.("VansRouter catalog resynced", "info"); return; }',
  '      if (sub === "repair") {',
  '        await writeCatalogWithBackup({ fetchedAt: Date.now(), source: "seed", models: SEED_MODELS });',
  '        await syncAndRegister(ctx, "repair");',
  '        ctx.ui?.notify?.("VansRouter cache repaired", "info");',
  '        return;',
  '      }',
  '      if (sub === "cache") {',
  '        const tiers = await Promise.all([CATALOG_MAIN, CATALOG_BAK1, CATALOG_BAK2].map(async (f) => {',
  '          try { const s = await fsp.stat(f); return path.basename(f) + ": " + s.size + "B @ " + new Date(s.mtimeMs).toISOString(); }',
  '          catch { return path.basename(f) + ": (absent)"; }',
  '        }));',
  '        ctx.ui?.notify?.(tiers.join("\\n"), "info");',
  '        return;',
  '      }',
  '      ctx.ui?.notify?.("usage: /vansrouter [status|sync|repair|cache]", "info");',
  '    },',
  '  });',
  '',
  '  pi.on("session_end", async () => {',
  '    if (lastCatalog) { try { await writeCatalogWithBackup(lastCatalog); } catch {} }',
  '  });',
  '}',
  ''
].join("\n");

const tmp = TARGET + ".tmp";
fs.writeFileSync(tmp, EXTENSION_SOURCE, { mode: 0o644 });
fs.renameSync(tmp, TARGET);

const size = fs.statSync(TARGET).size;
console.log("wrote " + TARGET + " (" + size + "B)");

say("3 verify backups");
for (const f of [BAK1, BAK2]) {
  try {
    const s = fs.statSync(f);
    console.log("  " + path.basename(f) + ": " + s.size + "B @ " + new Date(s.mtimeMs).toISOString());
  } catch {
    console.log("  " + path.basename(f) + ": (absent, first run)");
  }
}

say("4 type-check (best-effort)");
const tc = run("npx tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck extensions/vansrouter.ts 2>&1 | head -20", SRC);
console.log(tc.out || tc.err || "(clean)");

say("5 next steps");
console.log("  add to package.json:  \"omp\": { \"extensions\": [\"./extensions/vansrouter.ts\"] }");
console.log("  link:                 omp plugin link \"" + SRC + "\"");
console.log("  verify:               omp models find vansrouter");
console.log("  in-session:           /vansrouter status");
console.log("  env:                  echo \"VANSROUTER_API_KEY=$(cat ~/.9router/api.key)\" >> ~/.omp/agent/.env");
TS_EOF

bun run /tmp/write-vans-ext.ts

  '//   Discovery:  dynamic /v1/models -> disk cache (3 rotations) -> seed list',
  '//   Health:     /api/health -> /v1/models -> TCP connect -> unregistered',
  '//   Resilience: /api/breaker + /api/quota/kimchi + /api/proxies -> status only',
  '//   ACL:        /api/key/info -> unfiltered on failure',

  '// Uses pi.registerProvider + fetchDynamicModels + ctx.ui.* only.',
  '// No createProvider. No @earendil-works/* or @mariozechner/*.',
  '',
  'import type { ExtensionAPI } from "@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent";',
  'import { promises as fsp } from "node:fs";',
  'import path from "node:path";',
  'import os from "node:os";',
  'import net from "node:net";',
  '',
  'const VR_BASE = process.env.VANSROUTER_URL ?? process.env.NINEROUTER_URL ?? "http://127.0.0.1:20128";',
  'const VR_KEY_ENV = "VANSROUTER_API_KEY";',
  'const VR_KEY_FALLBACK_ENV = "NINEROUTER_KEY";',
  '',
  'const CACHE_DIR = path.join(os.homedir(), ".omp", "agent", "cache");',
  'const CATALOG_MAIN = path.join(CACHE_DIR, "vansrouter-catalog.json");',
  'const CATALOG_BAK1 = path.join(CACHE_DIR, "vansrouter-catalog.bak1.json");',
  'const CATALOG_BAK2 = path.join(CACHE_DIR, "vansrouter-catalog.bak2.json");',
  'const RESILIENCE_CACHE = path.join(CACHE_DIR, "vansrouter-resilience.json");',
  '',
  'const HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS = 3000;',
  'const HEALTH_TIMEOUT_MS = 1500;',
  'const DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT_MS = 8000;',
  '',
  'const SEED_MODELS = [',
  '  { id: "oc/jev-1.13-free", name: "OpenCode Jev Free", contextWindow: 128000, maxTokens: 8192 },',
  '  { id: "oc/mimo-v2.5-free", name: "OpenCode Mimo Free", contextWindow: 128000, maxTokens: 8192 },',
  '  { id: "oc/nemotron-3.5-lightning-free", name: "OpenCode Nemotron Lightning Free", contextWindow: 128000, maxTokens: 8192 },',
  '  { id: "oc/deepseek-v4-flash-free", name: "OpenCode DeepSeek Flash Free", contextWindow: 128000, maxTokens: 8192 },',
  '  { id: "mmf/mimo-auto", name: "MMF Mimo Auto", contextWindow: 128000, maxTokens: 8192 },',
  '];',
  '',
  'interface ModelEntry { id: string; name: string; contextWindow: number; maxTokens: number; }',
  'interface Catalog { fetchedAt: number; source: "dynamic" | "cache-main" | "cache-bak1" | "cache-bak2" | "seed"; models: ModelEntry[]; }',
  'interface ResilienceStatus {',
  '  fetchedAt: number;',
  '  breaker: { open?: number } | null;',
  '  quota: { daysUntilReset?: number } | null;',
  '  proxies: { dead?: number; pools?: number } | null;',
  '  acl: { allowedProviders?: string[]; allowedKinds?: string[] } | null;',
  '}',
  '',
  'async function httpJson<T>(url: string, init: RequestInit = {}, timeoutMs = HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS): Promise<T | null> {',
  '  try {',
  '    const res = await fetch(url, { ...init, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs) });',
  '    if (!res.ok) return null;',
  '    return (await res.json()) as T;',
  '  } catch { return null; }',
  '}',
  '',
  'function authHeaders(key: string): Record<string, string> {',
  '  return key ? { Authorization: "Bearer " + key } : {};',
  '}',
  '',
  'async function probeHealth(base: string): Promise<boolean> {',
  '  const h = await httpJson<{ ok?: boolean }>(base + "/api/health", {}, HEALTH_TIMEOUT_MS);',
  '  if (h && h.ok !== false) return true;',
  '  const m = await httpJson<unknown>(base + "/v1/models", {}, HEALTH_TIMEOUT_MS);',
  '  if (m) return true;',
  '  return tcpProbe(base);',
  '}',
  '',
  'function tcpProbe(base: string): Promise<boolean> {',
  '  return new Promise((resolve) => {',
  '    try {',
  '      const u = new URL(base);',
  '      const port = Number(u.port || (u.protocol === "https:" ? 443 : 80));',
  '      const sock = net.connect({ host: u.hostname, port }, () => { sock.destroy(); resolve(true); });',
  '      sock.on("error", () => { sock.destroy(); resolve(false); });',
  '      sock.setTimeout(1500, () => { sock.destroy(); resolve(false); });',
  '    } catch { resolve(false); }',
  '  });',
  '}',
  '',
  'async function fetchCatalogDynamic(base: string, key: string): Promise<ModelEntry[] | null> {',
  '  const body = await httpJson<{ data?: Array<Record<string, unknown>> }>(base + "/v1/models", { headers: authHeaders(key) }, DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT_MS);',
  '  if (!body?.data || !Array.isArray(body.data)) return null;',
  '  const seen = new Set<string>();',
  '  const out: ModelEntry[] = [];',
  '  for (const raw of body.data) {',
  '    const id = typeof raw.id === "string" ? raw.id : null;',
  '    if (!id || seen.has(id)) continue;',
  '    seen.add(id);',
  '    out.push({',
  '      id,',
  '      name: typeof raw.name === "string" ? raw.name : id,',
  '      contextWindow: typeof raw.context_window === "number" ? raw.context_window : typeof raw.contextWindow === "number" ? raw.contextWindow : 128000,',
  '      maxTokens: typeof raw.max_tokens === "number" ? raw.max_tokens : typeof raw.maxTokens === "number" ? raw.maxTokens : 8192,',
  '    });',
  '  }',
  '  return out.length ? out : null;',
  '}',
  '',
  'async function readCatalogFromDisk(): Promise<Catalog | null> {',
  '  const files: Array<[string, Catalog["source"]]> = [[CATALOG_MAIN, "cache-main"], [CATALOG_BAK1, "cache-bak1"], [CATALOG_BAK2, "cache-bak2"]];',
  '  for (const [f, src] of files) {',
  '    try {',
  '      const parsed = JSON.parse(await fsp.readFile(f, "utf8")) as Partial<Catalog>;',
  '      if (Array.isArray(parsed.models) && parsed.models.length > 0) {',
  '        return { fetchedAt: typeof parsed.fetchedAt === "number" ? parsed.fetchedAt : 0, source: src, models: parsed.models as ModelEntry[] };',
  '      }',
  '    } catch {}',
  '  }',
  '  return null;',
  '}',
  '',
  'async function writeCatalogWithBackup(catalog: Catalog): Promise<void> {',
  '  await fsp.mkdir(CACHE_DIR, { recursive: true });',
  '  try { await fsp.copyFile(CATALOG_MAIN, CATALOG_BAK1); } catch {}',
  '  try { await fsp.copyFile(CATALOG_BAK1, CATALOG_BAK2); } catch {}',
  '  const tmp = CATALOG_MAIN + ".tmp";',
  '  await fsp.writeFile(tmp, JSON.stringify(catalog, null, 2), { mode: 0o600 });',
  '  await fsp.rename(tmp, CATALOG_MAIN);',
  '}',
  '',
  'async function resolveCatalog(base: string, key: string): Promise<Catalog> {',
  '  const dyn = await fetchCatalogDynamic(base, key);',
  '  if (dyn) {',
  '    const c: Catalog = { fetchedAt: Date.now(), source: "dynamic", models: dyn };',
  '    await writeCatalogWithBackup(c);',
  '    return c;',
  '  }',
  '  const cached = await readCatalogFromDisk();',
  '  if (cached) return cached;',
  '  return { fetchedAt: Date.now(), source: "seed", models: SEED_MODELS };',
  '}',
  '',
  'async function probeResilience(base: string, key: string): Promise<ResilienceStatus> {',
  '  const h = authHeaders(key);',
  '  const [b, q, p, a] = await Promise.allSettled([',
  '    httpJson<ResilienceStatus["breaker"]>(base + "/api/breaker", { headers: h }),',
  '    httpJson<ResilienceStatus["quota"]>(base + "/api/quota/kimchi", { headers: h }),',
  '    httpJson<ResilienceStatus["proxies"]>(base + "/api/proxies", { headers: h }),',
  '    httpJson<ResilienceStatus["acl"]>(base + "/api/key/info", { headers: h }),',
  '  ]);',
  '  const pick = <T>(r: PromiseSettledResult<T | null>): T | null => r.status === "fulfilled" ? r.value : null;',
  '  const status: ResilienceStatus = { fetchedAt: Date.now(), breaker: pick(b), quota: pick(q), proxies: pick(p), acl: pick(a) };',
  '  try {',
  '    await fsp.mkdir(CACHE_DIR, { recursive: true });',
  '    await fsp.writeFile(RESILIENCE_CACHE, JSON.stringify(status, null, 2), { mode: 0o600 });',
  '  } catch {}',
  '  return status;',
  '}',
  '',
  'function applyAclFilter(models: ModelEntry[], acl: ResilienceStatus["acl"]): ModelEntry[] {',
  '  if (!acl) return models;',
  '  const { allowedProviders } = acl;',
  '  if (!allowedProviders) return models;',
  '  return models.filter((m) => allowedProviders.includes(m.id.split("/")[0]));',
  '}',
  '',
  'function formatStatusLine(catalog: Catalog, status: ResilienceStatus | null): string {',
  '  const parts: string[] = [];',
  '  const tag = catalog.source === "dynamic" ? "" : catalog.source.startsWith("cache") ? " (" + catalog.source.replace("cache-", "") + ")" : " (seed)";',
  '  parts.push("VR:" + catalog.models.length + tag);',
  '  if (status?.breaker?.open) parts.push(status.breaker.open + " tripped");',
  '  if (status?.quota?.daysUntilReset) parts.push(status.quota.daysUntilReset + "d reset");',
  '  if (status?.proxies?.dead) parts.push(status.proxies.dead + " dead");',
  '  return parts.join(" - ");',
  '}',
  '',
  'export default function vansrouterExtension(pi: ExtensionAPI) {',
  '  let lastCatalog: Catalog | null = null;',
  '  let lastStatus: ResilienceStatus | null = null;',
  '',
  '  function resolveKey(): string {',
  '    return process.env[VR_KEY_ENV] ?? process.env[VR_KEY_FALLBACK_ENV] ?? "";',
  '  }',
  '',
  '  async function syncAndRegister(ctx: any, reason: string): Promise<void> {',
  '    const healthy = await probeHealth(VR_BASE);',
  '    if (!healthy) {',
  '      ctx.ui?.notify?.("VansRouter unreachable at " + VR_BASE + " (" + reason + ")", "warn");',
  '      return;',
  '    }',
  '    const catalog = await resolveCatalog(VR_BASE, resolveKey());',
  '    lastCatalog = catalog;',
  '    const status = await probeResilience(VR_BASE, resolveKey());',
  '    lastStatus = status;',
  '    const filtered = applyAclFilter(catalog.models, status.acl);',
  '    const visible = filtered.length ? filtered : catalog.models;',
  '    pi.registerProvider("vansrouter", {',
  '      baseUrl: VR_BASE + "/v1",',
  '      apiKey: VR_KEY_ENV,',
  '      api: "openai-completions",',
  '      authHeader: true,',
  '      fetchDynamicModels: async (apiKey: string) => {',
  '        const dyn = await fetchCatalogDynamic(VR_BASE, apiKey);',
  '        if (dyn) {',
  '          const fd = applyAclFilter(dyn, lastStatus?.acl ?? null);',
  '          const vis = fd.length ? fd : dyn;',
  '          lastCatalog = { fetchedAt: Date.now(), source: "dynamic", models: vis };',
  '          await writeCatalogWithBackup(lastCatalog);',
  '          return vis;',
  '        }',
  '        return visible;',
  '      },',
  '    });',
  '    try { ctx.ui?.setStatus?.("vansrouter", formatStatusLine(catalog, status)); } catch {}',
  '  }',
  '',
  '  pi.on("session_start", async (_e: unknown, ctx: any) => { await syncAndRegister(ctx, "session_start"); });',
  '',
  '  pi.registerCommand?.("vansrouter", {',
  '    description: "VansRouter provider control",',
  '    handler: async (args: string, ctx: any) => {',
  '      const sub = (args || "").trim().split(/\\s+/)[0] || "status";',
  '      if (sub === "status") {',
  '        const cat = lastCatalog ?? (await readCatalogFromDisk()) ?? { fetchedAt: 0, source: "seed" as const, models: SEED_MODELS };',
  '        ctx.ui?.notify?.(formatStatusLine(cat, lastStatus) + "\\nbase: " + VR_BASE + "\\nkey: " + (resolveKey() ? "present" : "MISSING") + "\\nmodels: " + cat.models.map((m) => m.id).join(", "), "info");',
  '        return;',
  '      }',
  '      if (sub === "sync") { await syncAndRegister(ctx, "manual sync"); ctx.ui?.notify?.("VansRouter catalog resynced", "info"); return; }',
  '      if (sub === "repair") {',
  '        await writeCatalogWithBackup({ fetchedAt: Date.now(), source: "seed", models: SEED_MODELS });',
  '        await syncAndRegister(ctx, "repair");',
  '        ctx.ui?.notify?.("VansRouter cache repaired", "info");',
  '        return;',
  '      }',
  '      if (sub === "cache") {',
  '        const tiers = await Promise.all([CATALOG_MAIN, CATALOG_BAK1, CATALOG_BAK2].map(async (f) => {',
  '          try { const s = await fsp.stat(f); return path.basename(f) + ": " + s.size + "B @ " + new Date(s.mtimeMs).toISOString(); }',
  '          catch { return path.basename(f) + ": (absent)"; }',
  '        }));',
  '        ctx.ui?.notify?.(tiers.join("\\n"), "info");',
  '        return;',
  '      }',
  '      ctx.ui?.notify?.("usage: /vansrouter [status|sync|repair|cache]", "info");',
  '    },',
  '  });',
  '',
  '  pi.on("session_end", async () => {',
  '    if (lastCatalog) { try { await writeCatalogWithBackup(lastCatalog); } catch {} }',
  '  });',
  '}',
  ''
].join("\n");

const tmp = TARGET + ".tmp";
fs.writeFileSync(tmp, EXTENSION_SOURCE, { mode: 0o644 });
fs.renameSync(tmp, TARGET);

const size = fs.statSync(TARGET).size;
console.log("wrote " + TARGET + " (" + size + "B)");

say("3 verify backups");
for (const f of [BAK1, BAK2]) {
  try {
    const s = fs.statSync(f);
    console.log("  " + path.basename(f) + ": " + s.size + "B @ " + new Date(s.mtimeMs).toISOString());
  } catch {
    console.log("  " + path.basename(f) + ": (absent, first run)");
  }
}

say("4 type-check (best-effort)");
const tc = run("npx tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck extensions/vansrouter.ts 2>&1", SRC);
console.log(tc.out || tc.err || "(clean)");

say("5 next steps");
console.log("  add to package.json:  \"omp\": { \"extensions\": [\"./extensions/vansrouter.ts\"] }");
console.log("  link:                 omp plugin link \"" + SRC + "\"");
console.log("  verify:               omp models find vansrouter");

  '//   Health:     /api/health -> /v1/models -> TCP connect -> unregistered',
  '//   Resilience: /api/breaker + /api/quota/kimchi + /api/proxies -> status only',
  '//   ACL:        /api/key/info -> unfiltered on failure',
  '//   Write:      rotate main -> bak1 -> bak2, then atomic rename',
  '//',
  '// Uses pi.registerProvider + fetchDynamicModels + ctx.ui.* only.',
  '// No createProvider. No @earendil-works/* or @mariozechner/*.',
  '',
  'import type { ExtensionAPI } from "@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent";',
  'import { promises as fsp } from "node:fs";',
  'import path from "node:path";',
  'import os from "node:os";',
  'import net from "node:net";',
  '',
  'const VR_BASE = process.env.VANSROUTER_URL ?? process.env.NINEROUTER_URL ?? "http://127.0.0.1:20128";',
  'const VR_KEY_ENV = "VANSROUTER_API_KEY";',
  'const VR_KEY_FALLBACK_ENV = "NINEROUTER_KEY";',
  '',
  'const CACHE_DIR = path.join(os.homedir(), ".omp", "agent", "cache");',
  'const CATALOG_MAIN = path.join(CACHE_DIR, "vansrouter-catalog.json");',
  'const CATALOG_BAK1 = path.join(CACHE_DIR, "vansrouter-catalog.bak1.json");',
  'const CATALOG_BAK2 = path.join(CACHE_DIR, "vansrouter-catalog.bak2.json");',
  'const RESILIENCE_CACHE = path.join(CACHE_DIR, "vansrouter-resilience.json");',
  '',
  'const HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS = 3000;',
  'const HEALTH_TIMEOUT_MS = 1500;',
  'const DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT_MS = 8000;',
  '',
  'const SEED_MODELS = [',
  '  { id: "oc/jev-1.13-free", name: "OpenCode Jev Free", contextWindow: 128000, maxTokens: 8192 },',
  '  { id: "oc/mimo-v2.5-free", name: "OpenCode Mimo Free", contextWindow: 128000, maxTokens: 8192 },',
  '  { id: "oc/nemotron-3.5-lightning-free", name: "OpenCode Nemotron Lightning Free", contextWindow: 128000, maxTokens: 8192 },',
  '  { id: "oc/deepseek-v4-flash-free", name: "OpenCode DeepSeek Flash Free", contextWindow: 128000, maxTokens: 8192 },',
  '  { id: "mmf/mimo-auto", name: "MMF Mimo Auto", contextWindow: 128000, maxTokens: 8192 },',
  '];',
  '',
  'interface ModelEntry { id: string; name: string; contextWindow: number; maxTokens: number; }',
  'interface Catalog { fetchedAt: number; source: "dynamic" | "cache-main" | "cache-bak1" | "cache-bak2" | "seed"; models: ModelEntry[]; }',
  'interface ResilienceStatus {',
  '  fetchedAt: number;',
  '  breaker: { open?: number } | null;',
  '  quota: { daysUntilReset?: number } | null;',
  '  proxies: { dead?: number; pools?: number } | null;',
  '  acl: { allowedProviders?: string[]; allowedKinds?: string[] } | null;',
  '}',
  '',
  'async function httpJson<T>(url: string, init: RequestInit = {}, timeoutMs = HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS): Promise<T | null> {',
  '  try {',
  '    const res = await fetch(url, { ...init, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs) });',
  '    if (!res.ok) return null;',
  '    return (await res.json()) as T;',
  '  } catch { return null; }',
  '}',
  '',
  'function authHeaders(key: string): Record<string, string> {',
  '  return key ? { Authorization: "Bearer " + key } : {};',
  '}',
  '',
  'async function probeHealth(base: string): Promise<boolean> {',
  '  const h = await httpJson<{ ok?: boolean }>(base + "/api/health", {}, HEALTH_TIMEOUT_MS);',
  '  if (h && h.ok !== false) return true;',
  '  const m = await httpJson<unknown>(base + "/v1/models", {}, HEALTH_TIMEOUT_MS);',
  '  if (m) return true;',
  '  return tcpProbe(base);',
  '}',
  '',
  'function tcpProbe(base: string): Promise<boolean> {',
  '  return new Promise((resolve) => {',
  '    try {',
  '      const u = new URL(base);',
  '      const port = Number(u.port || (u.protocol === "https:" ? 443 : 80));',
  '      const sock = net.connect({ host: u.hostname, port }, () => { sock.destroy(); resolve(true); });',
  '      sock.on("error", () => { sock.destroy(); resolve(false); });',
  '      sock.setTimeout(1500, () => { sock.destroy(); resolve(false); });',
  '    } catch { resolve(false); }',
  '  });',
  '}',
  '',
  'async function fetchCatalogDynamic(base: string, key: string): Promise<ModelEntry[] | null> {',
  '  const body = await httpJson<{ data?: Array<Record<string, unknown>> }>(base + "/v1/models", { headers: authHeaders(key) }, DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT_MS);',
  '  if (!body?.data || !Array.isArray(body.data)) return null;',
  '  const seen = new Set<string>();',
  '  const out: ModelEntry[] = [];',
  '  for (const raw of body.data) {',
  '    const id = typeof raw.id === "string" ? raw.id : null;',
  '    if (!id || seen.has(id)) continue;',
  '    seen.add(id);',
  '    out.push({',
  '      id,',
  '      name: typeof raw.name === "string" ? raw.name : id,',
  '      contextWindow: typeof raw.context_window === "number" ? raw.context_window : typeof raw.contextWindow === "number" ? raw.contextWindow : 128000,',
  '      maxTokens: typeof raw.max_tokens === "number" ? raw.max_tokens : typeof raw.maxTokens === "number" ? raw.maxTokens : 8192,',
  '    });',
  '  }',
  '  return out.length ? out : null;',
  '}',
  '',
  'async function readCatalogFromDisk(): Promise<Catalog | null> {',
  '  const files: Array<[string, Catalog["source"]]> = [[CATALOG_MAIN, "cache-main"], [CATALOG_BAK1, "cache-bak1"], [CATALOG_BAK2, "cache-bak2"]];',
  '  for (const [f, src] of files) {',
  '    try {',
  '      const parsed = JSON.parse(await fsp.readFile(f, "utf8")) as Partial<Catalog>;',
  '      if (Array.isArray(parsed.models) && parsed.models.length > 0) {',
  '        return { fetchedAt: typeof parsed.fetchedAt === "number" ? parsed.fetchedAt : 0, source: src, models: parsed.models as ModelEntry[] };',
  '      }',
  '    } catch {}',
  '  }',
  '  return null;',
  '}',
  '',
  'async function writeCatalogWithBackup(catalog: Catalog): Promise<void> {',
  '  await fsp.mkdir(CACHE_DIR, { recursive: true });',
  '  try { await fsp.copyFile(CATALOG_MAIN, CATALOG_BAK1); } catch {}',
  '  try { await fsp.copyFile(CATALOG_BAK1, CATALOG_BAK2); } catch {}',
  '  const tmp = CATALOG_MAIN + ".tmp";',
  '  await fsp.writeFile(tmp, JSON.stringify(catalog, null, 2), { mode: 0o600 });',
  '  await fsp.rename(tmp, CATALOG_MAIN);',
  '}',
  '',
  'async function resolveCatalog(base: string, key: string): Promise<Catalog> {',
  '  const dyn = await fetchCatalogDynamic(base, key);',
  '  if (dyn) {',
  '    const c: Catalog = { fetchedAt: Date.now(), source: "dynamic", models: dyn };',
  '    await writeCatalogWithBackup(c);',
  '    return c;',
  '  }',
  '  const cached = await readCatalogFromDisk();',
  '  if (cached) return cached;',
  '  return { fetchedAt: Date.now(), source: "seed", models: SEED_MODELS };',
  '}',
  '',
  'async function probeResilience(base: string, key: string): Promise<ResilienceStatus> {',
  '  const h = authHeaders(key);',
  '  const [b, q, p, a] = await Promise.allSettled([',
  '    httpJson<ResilienceStatus["breaker"]>(base + "/api/breaker", { headers: h }),',
  '    httpJson<ResilienceStatus["quota"]>(base + "/api/quota/kimchi", { headers: h }),',
  '    httpJson<ResilienceStatus["proxies"]>(base + "/api/proxies", { headers: h }),',
  '    httpJson<ResilienceStatus["acl"]>(base + "/api/key/info", { headers: h }),',
  '  ]);',
  '  const pick = <T>(r: PromiseSettledResult<T | null>): T | null => r.status === "fulfilled" ? r.value : null;',
  '  const status: ResilienceStatus = { fetchedAt: Date.now(), breaker: pick(b), quota: pick(q), proxies: pick(p), acl: pick(a) };',
  '  try {',
  '    await fsp.mkdir(CACHE_DIR, { recursive: true });',
  '    await fsp.writeFile(RESILIENCE_CACHE, JSON.stringify(status, null, 2), { mode: 0o600 });',
  '  } catch {}',
  '  return status;',
  '}',
  '',
  'function applyAclFilter(models: ModelEntry[], acl: ResilienceStatus["acl"]): ModelEntry[] {',
  '  if (!acl) return models;',
  '  const { allowedProviders } = acl;',
  '  if (!allowedProviders) return models;',
  '  return models.filter((m) => allowedProviders.includes(m.id.split("/")[0]));',
  '}',
  '',
  'function formatStatusLine(catalog: Catalog, status: ResilienceStatus | null): string {',
  '  const parts: string[] = [];',
  '  const tag = catalog.source === "dynamic" ? "" : catalog.source.startsWith("cache") ? " (" + catalog.source.replace("cache-", "") + ")" : " (seed)";',
  '  parts.push("VR:" + catalog.models.length + tag);',
  '  if (status?.breaker?.open) parts.push(status.breaker.open + " tripped");',
  '  if (status?.quota?.daysUntilReset) parts.push(status.quota.daysUntilReset + "d reset");',
  '  if (status?.proxies?.dead) parts.push(status.proxies.dead + " dead");',
  '  return parts.join(" - ");',
  '}',
  '',
  'export default function vansrouterExtension(pi: ExtensionAPI) {',
  '  let lastCatalog: Catalog | null = null;',
  '  let lastStatus: ResilienceStatus | null = null;',
  '',
  '  function resolveKey(): string {',
  '    return process.env[VR_KEY_ENV] ?? process.env[VR_KEY_FALLBACK_ENV] ?? "";',
  '  }',
  '',
  '  async function syncAndRegister(ctx: any, reason: string): Promise<void> {',
  '    const healthy = await probeHealth(VR_BASE);',
  '    if (!healthy) {',
  '      ctx.ui?.notify?.("VansRouter unreachable at " + VR_BASE + " (" + reason + ")", "warn");',
  '      return;',
  '    }',
  '    const catalog = await resolveCatalog(VR_BASE, resolveKey());',
  '    lastCatalog = catalog;',
  '    const status = await probeResilience(VR_BASE, resolveKey());',
  '    lastStatus = status;',
  '    const filtered = applyAclFilter(catalog.models, status.acl);',
  '    const visible = filtered.length ? filtered : catalog.models;',
  '    pi.registerProvider("vansrouter", {',
  '      baseUrl: VR_BASE + "/v1",',
  '      apiKey: VR_KEY_ENV,',
  '      api: "openai-completions",',
  '      authHeader: true,',
  '      fetchDynamicModels: async (apiKey: string) => {',
  '        const dyn = await fetchCatalogDynamic(VR_BASE, apiKey);',
  '        if (dyn) {',
  '          const fd = applyAclFilter(dyn, lastStatus?.acl ?? null);',
  '          const vis = fd.length ? fd : dyn;',
  '          lastCatalog = { fetchedAt: Date.now(), source: "dynamic", models: vis };',
  '          await writeCatalogWithBackup(lastCatalog);',
  '          return vis;',
  '        }',
  '        return visible;',
  '      },',
  '    });',
  '    try { ctx.ui?.setStatus?.("vansrouter", formatStatusLine(catalog, status)); } catch {}',
  '  }',
  '',
  '  pi.on("session_start", async (_e: unknown, ctx: any) => { await syncAndRegister(ctx, "session_start"); });',
  '',
  '  pi.registerCommand?.("vansrouter", {',
  '    description: "VansRouter provider control",',
  '    handler: async (args: string, ctx: any) => {',
  '      const sub = (args || "").trim().split(/\\s+/)[0] || "status";',
  '      if (sub === "status") {',
  '        const cat = lastCatalog ?? (await readCatalogFromDisk()) ?? { fetchedAt: 0, source: "seed" as const, models: SEED_MODELS };',
  '        ctx.ui?.notify?.(formatStatusLine(cat, lastStatus) + "\\nbase: " + VR_BASE + "\\nkey: " + (resolveKey() ? "present" : "MISSING") + "\\nmodels: " + cat.models.map((m) => m.id).join(", "), "info");',
  '        return;',
  '      }',
  '      if (sub === "sync") { await syncAndRegister(ctx, "manual sync"); ctx.ui?.notify?.("VansRouter catalog resynced", "info"); return; }',
  '      if (sub === "repair") {',
  '        await writeCatalogWithBackup({ fetchedAt: Date.now(), source: "seed", models: SEED_MODELS });',
  '        await syncAndRegister(ctx, "repair");',
  '        ctx.ui?.notify?.("VansRouter cache repaired", "info");',
  '        return;',
  '      }',
  '      if (sub === "cache") {',
  '        const tiers = await Promise.all([CATALOG_MAIN, CATALOG_BAK1, CATALOG_BAK2].map(async (f) => {',
  '          try { const s = await fsp.stat(f); return path.basename(f) + ": " + s.size + "B @ " + new Date(s.mtimeMs).toISOString(); }',
  '          catch { return path.basename(f) + ": (absent)"; }',
  '        }));',
  '        ctx.ui?.notify?.(tiers.join("\\n"), "info");',
  '        return;',
  '      }',
  '      ctx.ui?.notify?.("usage: /vansrouter [status|sync|repair|cache]", "info");',
  '    },',
  '  });',
  '',
  '  pi.on("session_end", async () => {',
  '    if (lastCatalog) { try { await writeCatalogWithBackup(lastCatalog); } catch {} }',
  '  });',
  '}',
  ''
].join("\n");

const tmp = TARGET + ".tmp";
fs.writeFileSync(tmp, EXTENSION_SOURCE, { mode: 0o644 });
fs.renameSync(tmp, TARGET);

const size = fs.statSync(TARGET).size;
console.log("wrote " + TARGET + " (" + size + "B)");

say("3 verify backups");
for (const f of [BAK1, BAK2]) {
  try {
    const s = fs.statSync(f);
    console.log("  " + path.basename(f) + ": " + s.size + "B @ " + new Date(s.mtimeMs).toISOString());
  } catch {
    console.log("  " + path.basename(f) + ": (absent, first run)");
  }
}

say("4 type-check (best-effort)");
const tc = run("npx tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck extensions/vansrouter.ts 2>&1", SRC);
console.log(tc.out || tc.err || "(clean)");

say("5 next steps");
console.log("  add to package.json:  \"omp\": { \"extensions\": [\"./extensions/vansrouter.ts\"] }");
console.log("  link:                 omp plugin link \"" + SRC + "\"");
console.log("  verify:               omp models find vansrouter");
console.log("  in-session:           /vansrouter status");
console.log("  env:                  echo \"VANSROUTER_API_KEY=$(cat ~/.9router/api.key)\" >> ~/.omp/agent/.env");
TS_EOF", "i": "Write the VansRouter extension script to temp file"}

Inline functions whose whole body: one expression or `return`, unless name creates a durable contract.

## Why

- One-line wrappers: no real behavior.
- Readers: jump to verify trivial code.
- Signature: freezes shape too early.
- Inline expressions: better search and type flow.

## Avoid

```typescript
// Bad — pure rename, no behavior added.
function isEmpty(value: string): boolean {
	return value.length === 0;
}

const getDisplayName = (user: User) => user.profile.displayName;

function double(value: number) {
	return value * 2;
}

if (isEmpty(name)) { ... }
```

## Use

```typescript
if (name.length === 0) { ... }
const displayName = user.profile.displayName;
const doubled = value * 2;
```

## Allowed tiny functions

- Three or more call sites need lockstep behavior.
- Exported name: stable domain concept.
- Callback identity matters.
- Type guard preserves narrowing.
- Public API, test seam, or DI boundary needs indirection.
- Names non-obvious formula or magic-constant computation the inlined expression would not explain alone.

If none apply, inline it.
</system-reminder>

<system-reminder reason="rule_violation" rule="ts-promise-with-resolvers" path="builtin-defaults:ts-promise-with-resolvers.md">

Prefer `Promise.withResolvers()` over `new Promise((resolve, reject) => ...)`: linear control flow; typed resolvers without callback nesting.

## Basic operation

```typescript
// Bad
function delay(ms: number): Promise<void> {
	return new Promise(resolve => {
		setTimeout(resolve, ms);
	});
}

// Good
function delay(ms: number): Promise<void> {
	const { promise, resolve } = Promise.withResolvers<void>();
	setTimeout(resolve, ms);
	return promise;
}
```

## Event-based completion

```typescript
// Bad
function waitForEvent(emitter: EventEmitter, event: string): Promise<unknown> {
	return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
		emitter.once(event, resolve);
		emitter.once("error", reject);
	});
}

// Good
function waitForEvent(emitter: EventEmitter, event: string): Promise<unknown> {
	const { promise, resolve, reject } = Promise.withResolvers<unknown>();
	emitter.once(event, resolve);
	emitter.once("error", reject);
	return promise;
}
```

## Stored resolver

```typescript
class Gate {
	#promise: Promise<void>;
	#resolve: () => void;

	constructor() {
		const { promise, resolve } = Promise.withResolvers<void>();
		this.#promise = promise;
		this.#resolve = resolve;
	}

	open(): void { this.#resolve(); }
	wait(): Promise<void> { return this.#promise; }
}
```

Constructor only if an API specifically requires executor form.
</system-reminder>

Never use `: any` or `as any`. They disable type checking exactly where the boundary needs precision.

## Use instead

- `unknown` for unvalidated input.
- A schema parse (Zod, Valibot, …; e.g. Zod v4 when it is already in the project) for untrusted or external input — validate once, then consume a typed value.
- A domain type when the shape is known.
- A generic when the caller supplies the shape.
- A type guard when runtime checks establish shape.
- `satisfies` for object literals that must match a contract.

## Parameters and returns

```typescript
// Bad
function readId(value: any): any {
	return value.id;
}

// Good — validate unknown input.
function readId(value: unknown): string | undefined {
```

```typescript

root.innerText = "ready";

// Good
const root = document.getElementById("root") as HTMLElement | null;
root?.innerText = "ready";
```

```typescript

// Good
```

|---|---|

17|### Lifecycle & Safety

69|## Writing Extensions
70|
71|See [docs/extensions.md](../../docs/extensions.md) for full documentation.
72|
73|```typescript
74|import type { ExtensionAPI } from "@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent";
75|
76|export default function (pi: ExtensionAPI) {
77|	const z = pi.zod;
78|
79|	// Subscribe to lifecycle events
80|	pi.on("tool_call", async (event, ctx) => {
81|		if (event.toolName === "bash" && event.input.command?.includes("rm -rf")) {
82|			const ok = await ctx.ui.confirm("Dangerous!", "Allow rm -rf?");
83|			if (!ok) return { block: true, reason: "Blocked by user" };
84|		}
85|	});
86|
87|	// Register custom tools
88|	pi.registerTool({
89|		name: "greet",
90|		label: "Greeting",
91|		description: "Generate a greeting",
92|		parameters: z.object({
93|			name: z.string().describe("Name to greet"),
94|		}),
95|		async execute(toolCallId, params, onUpdate, ctx, signal) {
96|			return {
97|				content: [{ type: "text", text: `Hello, ${params.name}!` }],
98|				details: {},
99|			};
100|		},
101|	});
102|
103|	// Register commands
104|	pi.registerCommand("hello", {
105|		description: "Say hello",
106|		handler: async (args, ctx) => {
107|			ctx.ui.notify("Hello!", "info");
108|		},
109|	});
110|}
111|```
112|

114|
115|**Use `z.enum` for discriminated string tool args:**
116|
117|```typescript
118|const z = pi.zod;
119|
120|parameters: z.object({
121|	action: z.enum(["list", "add"]),
122|});
123|```
124|
125|**State persistence via details:**
126|
127|```typescript
128|// Store state in tool result details for proper branching support
129|return {
130|	content: [{ type: "text", text: "Done" }],
131|	details: { todos: [...todos], nextId }, // Persisted in session
132|};
133|
134|// Reconstruct on session events
135|pi.on("session_start", async (_event, ctx) => {
136|	for (const entry of ctx.sessionManager.getBranch()) {
137|		if (entry.type === "message" && entry.message.toolName === "my_tool") {
138|			const details = entry.message.details;
139|			// Reconstruct state from details
140|		}
141|	}
142|});

- `VANSROUTER_API_KEY` / `NINEROUTER_KEY` - API key for authenticated requests

This PR fixes Muse Spark integration in the Hermes Agent prompt enforcement. It expands the tool-use enforcement model lists to properly gate Muse Spark (muse/spark/claude/mimo) and ensure mandatory tool usage and execution guidance when enabled.

Key points:
- Problem: Muse Spark variants were not included in TOOL_USE_ENFORCEMENT_MODELS or EXECUTION_GUIDANCE_MODELS, causing default behavior to skip tool calls and finish prematurely.
- Change: Add Muse Spark family to:
  - TOOL_USE_ENFORCEMENT_MODELS: "muse", "claude", "spark", "mimo"
  - EXECUTION_GUIDANCE_MODELS: "muse", "spark" (mimo already present)
- Rationale: Align with other model families (gpt, deepseek, qwen, glm, minimax, mimo) and fix early-termination behavior for Muse Spark users.
- Verification: Reproduced absence of tool calls without the fix; with fix and verify_on_stop: auto, proper tool-enforcement and guidance blocks are applied; tests show 69/69 in relevant suite; gateway behavior now completes tasks rather than stopping early.
- Files touched: agent/prompt_builder.py (2 insertions, 1 deletion; tuple additions only)

If you’re specifically querying how Muse Spark is now treated for tool enforcement, the answer is: Muse Spark is now explicitly included in both TOOL_USE_ENFORCEMENT_MODELS and EXECUTION_GUIDANCE_MODELS, ensuring mandatory tool use and persistence/verification behaviors for Muse Spark prompts.

**Muse Spark early termination on defaults — not covered by TOOL_USE_ENFORCEMENT_MODELS / EXECUTION_GUIDANCE_MODELS**: Summary:
- Issue: muse-spark-1.2-contributor terminates early on defaults due to tool-use enforcement not recognizing Muse Spark model variants.
- Problem: TOOL_USE_ENFORCEMENT_MODELS and EXECUTION_GUIDANCE_MODELS use substring matching; names like muse-spark are not matched, so no guidance blocks are injected. Result: single-turn, no tool calls, gateway returns a short prose answer.
- Workaround: Enable enforcement unconditionally in config.yaml (tool_use_enforcement: true, execution_guidance: true) to force guidance blocks regardless of model name.
- Proposed fix (PR #96549): add Muse-related substrings to model lists:

  - EXECUTION_GUIDANCE_MODELS: include "muse", "spark" (plus existing names)

**fix(agent): include Muse Spark (muse/spark/claude/mimo) in prompt enforcement**: Summary:
This PR fixes Muse Spark integration in the Hermes Agent prompt enforcement. It expands the tool-use enforcement model lists to properly gate Muse Spark (muse/spark/claude/mimo) and ensure mandatory tool usage and execution guidance when enabled.

Key points:
- Problem: Muse Spark variants were not included in TOOL_USE_ENFORCEMENT_MODELS or EXECUTION_GUIDANCE_MODELS, causing default behavior to skip tool calls and finish prematurely.
- Change: Add Muse Spark family to:
  - TOOL_USE_ENFORCEMENT_MODELS: "muse", "claude", "spark", "mimo"
  - EXECUTION_GUIDANCE_MODELS: "muse", "spark" (mimo already present)
- Rationale: Align with other model families (gpt, deepseek, qwen, glm, minimax, mimo) and fix early-termination behavior for Muse Spark users.
- Verification: Reproduced absence of tool calls without the fix; with fix and verify_on_stop: auto, proper tool-enforcement and guidance blocks are applied; tests show 69/69 in relevant suite; gateway behavior now completes tasks rather than stopping early.
- Files touched: agent/prompt_builder.py (2 insertions, 1 deletion; tuple additions only)

If you’re specifically querying how Muse Spark is now treated for tool enforcement, the answer is: Muse Spark is now explicitly included in both TOOL_USE_ENFORCEMENT_MODELS and EXECUTION_GUIDANCE_MODELS, ensuring mandatory tool use and persistence/verification behaviors for Muse Spark prompts.

**Muse Spark early termination on defaults — not covered by TOOL_USE_ENFORCEMENT_MODELS / EXECUTION_GUIDANCE_MODELS**: Summary:
- Issue: muse-spark-1.2-contributor terminates early on defaults due to tool-use enforcement not recognizing Muse Spark model variants.
- Problem: TOOL_USE_ENFORCEMENT_MODELS and EXECUTION_GUIDANCE_MODELS use substring matching; names like muse-spark are not matched, so no guidance blocks are injected. Result: single-turn, no tool calls, gateway returns a short prose answer.
- Workaround: Enable enforcement unconditionally in config.yaml (tool_use_enforcement: true, execution_guidance: true) to force guidance blocks regardless of model name.
- Proposed fix (PR #96549): add Muse-related substrings to model lists:
  - TOOL_USE_ENFORCEMENT_MODELS: include "muse", "claude", "spark", "mimo" (and keep others)
  - EXECUTION_GUIDANCE_MODELS: include "muse", "spark" (plus existing names)
- Verification: After fix, guidance blocks are injected for auto mode; tests (pytest) pass in the fix branch.
- Follow-up context: Part of Muse Spark bundle improvements and related prompt enforcement updates.

User query focus: clarifies Muse Spark tool-use enforcement behavior and the model lists involved. The key detail is the missing substrings causing enforcement not to trigger and the exact proposed model-list changes.

- The commit fix(agent): add qwen and deepseek to TOOL_USE_ENFORCEMENT_MODELS updates the agent’s tool-use enforcement to include two additional model families: Qwen (qwen) and DeepSeek (deepseek).
- Purpose: Qwen3.x and DeepSeek-V3.x tend to be chatty/hallucinatory about tool usage without actual tool calls; adding them to TOOL_USE_ENFORCEMENT_MODELS ensures enforcement guidance is applied for these models as with other families (gpt, codex, gemini, gemma, grok, glm).
- Key changes:

  - Tests:

    - Added tests to verify enforcement guidance is injected for qwen and deepseek.
  - Tests coverage: Updated test_run_agent.py to ensure system prompts include TOOL_USE_ENFORCEMENT_GUIDANCE for qwen and deepseek when auto-enforcement is used.
- Impact: Ensures consistent enforcement behavior for Qwen and DeepSeek models, preventing partial tool-use loops and improving reliability of tool calls for these families.

**https://dev.meta.ai/docs/reasoning/**: Summary:
Muse Spark is a reasoning model that can generate internal reasoning tokens. You control the depth of reasoning with the reasoning_effort parameter at the top level of chat completions (or nested under reasoning.effort for the Responses API). Available levels: none (not supported by Muse Spark; returns HTTP 400), minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh. Higher values yield deeper reasoning, more tokens, latency, and cost. If you omit the parameter, a model-determined level is used. For direct-answer tasks, use low to balance speed and cost. The page provides code examples for both Chat Completions and the Responses API in various languages, showing how to set reasoning_effort and how to structure requests.

**https://dev.meta.ai/docs/features/reasoning/**: Summary:
The Muse Spark reasoning model supports adjustable reasoning depth via the reasoning_effort parameter. Available levels are none (not supported; returns HTTP 400), minimal, low, medium, high, and xhigh. Higher values increase internal reasoning tokens, latency, and cost; lower values are faster and cheaper. Key guidance:
- Use reasoning_effort at the top level for Chat Completions; nest under reasoning.effort for the Responses API.
- If you want a direct answer, start with lower reasoning (e.g., "low" or "minimal") for speed; reserve higher levels for deeper problem solving.
- Muse Spark does not support logprobs. Include appropriate reasoning effort to balance latency, cost, and depth.

**https://ai.developer.meta.com/docs/models**: Summary:
- Meta’s Muse Spark is a family of agentic/coding-focused models available via Meta Model API. It supports multi-step tool use, browser-based workflows, and long-context reasoning.
- Versions and tiers:
  - Muse Spark 1.3 (muse-spark-1.3): latest; best for agentic workflows and long-horizon tasks; supports all reasoning levels, including max (extended reasoning) on Standard tier; recommended for new work.
  - Muse Spark 1.2 (muse-spark-1.2): previous version.
  - Muse Spark 1.1 (muse-spark-1.1): original version.
  - Contributor variants: muse-spark-1.3-contributor and muse-spark-1.2-contributor, offering a training-on-prompts/completions option at a discount (permitting training on data). Standard tier pricing applies; contributor tier has different terms.
- Modalities and outputs:
  - Input: text, image, video, audio, PDF (vary by version)
  - Output: text
  - Context window: 1,048,576 tokens for all Spark 1.x variants
- Other Muse families:
  - Muse Image and Muse Voice Transcribe are hosted on Meta Model API.
  - Muse Glimmer is open-weight and runs on your own hardware.
- Next steps:
  - See pricing and rate limits docs for tier-specific costs.
  - Explore detailed docs for chat completions, image/video understanding, tool calling, structured output, and search grounding to implement your use case.

sources.title: Muse Spark 1.3 Asks Before It Acts. Fewer Tokens, Really?
sources.snippet:
Summary:
- Muse Spark 1.3, released by Meta, introduces a "asks before it acts" behavior and claims efficiency gains.
- Meta's internal (vendor-run) tests on coding workflows show about 20% fewer tool calls and 25% fewer tokens than Spark 1.2.
- Independent testing by Artificial Analysis on a fixed task set shows opposite figures: ~57% more input tokens per task (and ~8% more output tokens), raising cost per task from $0.40 to $0.55.
- The discrepancy arises from different measurement approaches

Note that output and input share the model’s context window: input_tokens plus requested output tokens must fit within the context window. Do not set max_completion_tokens to the full context window when input is present, or you may receive HTTP 400.

The Muse Spark chat completion endpoint supports models listed in the model availability page. Key parameter: max_completion_tokens (alias max_tokens deprecated) controls how many output tokens are generated, subject to the model’s context window. The input tokens and requested output tokens share the same context window, so do not set max_completion_tokens to the full context when input is present. Requests exceeding the model’s configured maximum return HTTP 400. Output tokens and input tokens must fit within the context window.

- The Meta AI chat model API uses max_completion_tokens (integer) to cap generated output. The deprecated alias max_tokens is still accepted.
- max_output_tokens is a separate parameter used in the Responses API and is not applicable to Chat Completions.
- Important constraint: input_tokens plus requested output tokens must fit within the model’s context window. Do not set max_completion_tokens to the full context window because input and output share the same budget.

content.text:
1|# Extension Loading (TypeScript/JavaScript Modules)
2|
3|This document covers how the coding agent discovers and loads extension modules at startup. Scanned native/configured directories auto-discover `.ts` and `.js`; explicitly named files and installed-plugin manifest entries may also use `.mjs` and `.cjs`.
4|
5|It does **not** cover [`gemini-extension.json` manifest extensions](./gemini-manifest-extensions.md), which are documented separately.
6|
7|## What this subsystem does
8|
9|Extension loading builds a list of module entry files, imports each module with Bun, executes its factory, and returns:
10|
11|- loaded extension definitions
12|- per-path load errors (without aborting the whole load)
13|- a shared extension runtime object used later by `ExtensionRunner`
14|
15|## Primary implementation files
16|
17|- `src/extensibility/extensions/loader.ts` — path discovery + import/execution
18|- `src/extensibility/extensions/index.ts` — public exports
19|- `src/extensibility/extensions/runner.ts` — runtime/event execution after load
20|- `src/discovery/builtin.ts` — native auto-discovery provider for extension modules
21|- `src/extensibility/plugins/legacy-pi-compat.ts` — in-place module graph loading and host-package compatibility rewriting
22|- `src/config/settings.ts` — loads merged `extensions` / `disabledExtensions` settings
23|
24|---
25|
26|## Inputs to extension loading
27|
28|### 1) Auto-discovered native extension modules
29|
30|`discoverAndLoadExtensions()` first asks discovery providers for `extension-module` capability items, then keeps only provider `native` items.
31|
32|Native `extension-module` discovery comes from:
33|
34|- Project directory: `<cwd>/.tau/extensions`
35|- User directory: the active agent directory's `extensions/` (default `~/.tau/agent/extensions`)
36|- Native legacy/settings JSON entries: `<cwd>/.tau/settings.json#extensions` and the active agent directory's `settings.json#extensions`
37|
38|The project root is the native provider's `.omp` directory (`SOURCE_PATHS.native.projectDir`), cwd-only; it does not walk ancestors. The user root is the active profile's agent directory via `getAgentDir()`, so under `omp --profile <name>` it becomes `~/.tau/profiles/<name>/agent/extensions` (and it honors `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`). See [Profiles](./config-usage.md#profiles).
39|
40|Notes:
41|
42|- Native auto-discovery is currently `.omp` based.
43|- Legacy `.pi` is still accepted in package manifests (`pi.extensions`) and project override lookup, but `.pi/extensions` is not a native root here.
44|
45|### 2) Discovered JS/TS hook factories
46|
47|After native auto-discovery, `discoverAndLoadExtensions()` also appends JS/TS hook factories from the `hook` capability — any hook whose entry path is a `.ts`/`.js` file — so they load through the same module pipeline.
48|
49|Hook-capability loading already applies its own hook-specific disabled ids, so these paths are not additionally filtered by `disabledExtensions` extension-module names.
50|
51|### 3) Installed plugin extension entries
52|
53|After hook discovery, `discoverAndLoadExtensions()` appends extension entry points from enabled installed plugins via `getAllPluginExtensionPaths(cwd)`.
54|
55|Plugin extension entries come from package `omp.extensions` / `pi.extensions` manifests, including enabled feature entries.
56|
57|Installed-plugin manifest resolution accepts explicit `.ts`, `.js`, `.mjs`, and `.cjs` files. For a manifest entry that names a directory, it recognizes `index.ts`, `index.js`, `index.mjs`, or `index.cjs`; extension-directory expansion uses the same four suffixes. This is broader than native and configured-directory auto-scanning, which remains limited to `.ts` and `.js`.
58|
59|### 4) Explicitly configured paths
60|
61|After plugin extension entries, configured paths are appended and resolved.
62|
63|Configured path sources in the main session startup path (`sdk.ts`):
64|
65|1. CLI-provided paths (`--extension/-e`, and `--hook` is also treated as an extension path)
66|2. Merged settings `extensions` array
67|
68|Settings files:
69|

# Extension Loading (TypeScript/JavaScript Modules)

This document covers how the coding agent discovers and loads extension modules at startup. Scanned native/configured directories auto-discover `.ts` and `.js`; explicitly named files and installed-plugin manifest entries may also use `.mjs` and `.cjs`.

It does **not** cover [`gemini-extension.json` manifest extensions](./gemini-manifest-extensions.md), which are documented separately.

## What this subsystem does

Extension loading builds a list of module entry files, imports each module with Bun, executes its factory, and returns:

- loaded extension definitions
- per-path load errors (without aborting the whole load)
- a shared extension runtime object used later by `ExtensionRunner`

## Primary implementation files

- `src/extensibility/extensions/loader.ts` — path discovery + import/execution
- `src/extensibility/extensions/index.ts` — public exports
- `src/extensibility/extensions/runner.ts` — runtime/event execution after load
- `src/discovery/builtin.ts` — native auto-discovery provider for extension modules
- `src/extensibility/plugins/legacy-pi-compat.ts` — in-place module graph loading and host-package compatibility rewriting
- `src/config/settings.ts` — loads merged `extensions` / `disabledExtensions` settings

---

## Inputs to extension loading

### 1) Auto-discovered native extension modules

`discoverAndLoadExtensions()` first asks discovery providers for `extension-module` capability items, then keeps only provider `native` items.

Native `extension-module` discovery comes from:

- Project directory: `<cwd>/.tau/extensions`
- User directory: the active agent directory's `extensions/` (default `~/.tau/agent/extensions`)
- Native legacy/settings JSON entries: `<cwd>/.tau/settings.json#extensions` and the active agent directory's `settings.json#extensions`

The project root is the native provider's `.omp` directory (`SOURCE_PATHS.native.projectDir`), cwd-only; it does not walk ancestors. The user root is the active profile's agent directory via `getAgentDir()`, so under `omp --profile <name>` it becomes `~/.tau/profiles/<name>/agent/extensions` (and it honors `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`). See [Profiles](./config-usage.md#profiles).

Notes:

- Native auto-discovery is currently `.omp` based.
- Legacy `.pi` is still accepted in package manifests (`pi.extensions`) and project override lookup, but `.pi/extensions` is not a native root here.

### 2) Discovered JS/TS hook factories

After native auto-discovery, `discoverAndLoadExtensions()` also appends JS/TS hook factories from the `hook` capability — any hook whose entry path is a `.ts`/`.js` file — so they load through the same module pipeline.

Hook-capability loading already applies its own hook-specific disabled ids, so these paths are not additionally filtered by `disabledExtensions` extension-module names.

### 3) Installed plugin extension entries

After hook discovery, `discoverAndLoadExtensions()` appends extension entry points from enabled installed plugins via `getAllPluginExtensionPaths(cwd)`.

Plugin extension entries come from package `omp.extensions` / `pi.extensions` manifests, including enabled feature entries.

Installed-plugin manifest resolution accepts explicit `.ts`, `.js`, `.mjs`, and `.cjs` files. For a manifest entry that names a directory, it recognizes `index.ts`, `index.js`, `index.mjs`, or `index.cjs`; extension-directory expansion uses the same four suffixes. This is broader than native and configured-directory auto-scanning, which remains limited to `.ts` and `.js`.

### 4) Explicitly configured paths

After plugin extension entries, configured paths are appended and resolved.

Configured path sources in the main session startup path (`sdk.ts`):

1. CLI-provided paths (`--extension/-e`, and `--hook` is also treated as an extension path)
2. Merged settings `extensions` array

Settings files:

- User: the active agent directory's `config.yml` (default `~/.tau/agent/config.yml`; with `--profile <name>`, `~/.tau/profiles/<name>/agent/config.yml`; `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` can override the agent directory)
- Project/native settings capability: `<cwd>/.tau/config.yml` and `<cwd>/.tau/settings.json`

Native extension-module discovery also reads legacy JSON extension lists from:

- The active agent directory's `settings.json` (default `~/.tau/agent/settings.json`)
- `<cwd>/.tau/settings.json`

Examples:

```yaml
# ~/.tau/agent/config.yml
extensions:
  - ~/my-exts/safety.ts
  - ./local/ext-pack
```

```json
{
  "extensions": ["./.tau/extensions/my-extra"]
}
```

---

## Enable/disable controls

### Disable discovery

- CLI: `--no-extensions`
- SDK option: `disableExtensionDiscovery`

Behavior split:

- SDK: when `disableExtensionDiscovery=true`, ambient extension factories are
  excluded, while `additionalExtensionPaths` are still resolved normally
  (including package directories with `package.json#omp.extensions`).
- CLI: `--no-extensions` follows the same explicit-only contract. Explicit
  `-e/--extension` and `--hook` paths still load, and only sibling capability
  roots from explicitly named extension packages remain eligible. Project/user
  `extensions:` settings and installed OMP extension packages are excluded from
  that sibling surface.

This flag governs extension factories and OMP extension-package sibling roots;
it is not a whole-process capability-isolation switch. Skills, MCP servers,
tools, prompts, and rules owned by other discovery subsystems retain their own
enable/disable controls.

### Disable specific extension modules

`disabledExtensions` setting filters by extension id format:

- `extension-module:<derivedName>`

`derivedName` is based on entry path (`getExtensionNameFromPath`), for example:

- `/x/foo.ts` -> `foo`
- `/x/bar/index.ts` -> `bar`

Example:

```yaml
disabledExtensions:
  - extension-module:foo
```

### Disable specific items of other capabilities

`disabledExtensions` is not limited to extension modules. Every capability that
defines `toExtensionId` contributes ids to the same list, and loading filters
them out before the item reaches the session.

Context files use `context-file:<level>:<basename>`, where `<level>` is `user`
or `project`:

```yaml
disabledExtensions:
  - context-file:user:CLAUDE.md
```

The id carries no directory and no depth, so a `project` entry disables files of
that name at every depth the discovery walk reaches. See
[Context files](./context-files.md#disabling-a-single-context-file).

---

## Path and entry resolution

### Path normalization

For configured paths:

1. Normalize Unicode spaces and supported path shorthands (including `file://`, `@/absolute/path`, and a stray `:` before an absolute/relative path)
2. Expand `~`
3. If relative, resolve against current `cwd`
4. Reject the internal `local://` scheme; it must be resolved by its protocol handler, not treated as a filesystem path

### If configured path is a file

It is used directly as a module entry candidate. Explicit `.ts`, `.js`, `.mjs`, and `.cjs` files are supported.

### If configured path is a directory

Resolution order:

1. `package.json` in that directory with `omp.extensions` (or legacy `pi.extensions`) -> use declared entries
2. `index.ts`
3. `index.js`
4. Otherwise scan one level for extension entries:
   - direct `*.ts` / `*.js`
   - subdir `index.ts` / `index.js`
   - subdir `package.json` with `omp.extensions` / `pi.extensions`

Rules and constraints:

- no recursive discovery beyond one subdirectory level
- declared `extensions` manifest entries are resolved relative to that package directory
- declared entries are included only if file exists/access is allowed
- in `*/index.{ts,js}` pairs, TypeScript is preferred over JavaScript
- symlinks are treated as eligible files/directories

### Ignore behavior differs by source

- Native auto-discovery (`discoverExtensionModulePaths` in discovery helpers) uses native glob with `gitignore: true` and `hidden: false`.
- Explicit configured directory scanning in `loader.ts` uses `readdir` rules and does **not** apply gitignore filtering.

---

## Load order and precedence

`discoverAndLoadExtensions()` builds one ordered list and then calls `loadExtensions()`.

Order:

1. Native auto-discovered modules
2. Discovered JS/TS hook factories
3. Installed plugin extension entries
4. Explicit configured paths (in provided order)

In `sdk.ts`, configured order is:

1. CLI additional paths
2. Settings `extensions`

De-duplication:

- absolute path based
- first seen path wins
- later duplicates are ignored

Implication: if the same module path is both auto-discovered and explicitly configured, it is loaded once at the first position (auto-discovered stage).

---

## Module import and factory contract

Each candidate path is loaded via `loadLegacyPiModule()` (`src/extensibility/plugins/legacy-pi-compat.ts`):

- the entry's realpath is resolved, then dynamically imported with an `?mtime` cache-buster so edited source reloads
- a scoped Bun `onLoad` hook rewrites legacy pi-package specifiers (`@mariozechner/*`, `@earendil-works/*`) and bare `@sinclair/typebox` onto the host-bundled copies before evaluation
- factory is selected by `getExtensionFactory(module)`: the module itself if it is a function, otherwise `module.default`
- factory must be a function (`ExtensionFactory`) and may return `void` or a promise; loading awaits it before continuing to the next path

If export is not a function, that path fails with a structured error and loading continues.

---

## Failure handling and isolation

### During loading

Per extension path, failures are captured as `{ path, error }` and do not stop other paths from loading.

Common cases:

- import failure / missing file
- invalid factory export (non-function)
- exception thrown while executing factory

### Runtime isolation model

- Extensions are **not sandboxed** (same process/runtime).
- They share one `EventBus` and one `ExtensionRuntime` instance.
- During load, runtime action methods intentionally throw `ExtensionRuntimeNotInitializedError`; action wiring happens later in `ExtensionRunner.initialize()`.

### After loading

When events run through `ExtensionRunner`, handler exceptions are caught and emitted as extension errors instead of crashing the runner loop.

---

## Minimal user/project layout examples

### User-level

```text
~/.tau/agent/
  config.yml
  extensions/
    guardrails.ts
    audit/
      index.ts
```

### Project-level

```text
<repo>/
  .tau/
    settings.json
    extensions/
      checks/
        package.json
      lint-gates.ts
```

`checks/package.json`:

```json
{
  "omp": {
    "extensions": ["./src/check-a.ts", "./src/check-b.js"]
  }
}
```

Legacy manifest key still accepted:

```json
{
  "pi": {
    "extensions": ["./index.ts"]
  }
}
```

Stop. Four separate faults stacked, and only fixing all four makes it load. The agent/ folder is not a discovery root — that's the first fault, and it is why the file has never executed.

The four faults

# Fault Evidence
1 Wrong language Tau extensions are Python modules. The file is TypeScript.
2 Wrong API surface The file calls pi.registerProvider(...). Provider registration is an explicit non-goal in Tau's Phase 21 extensions — the reserved name exists but has no implementation.
3 Wrong discovery path File is at ~/.tau/agent/extensions/. Tau's discovery roots are <cwd>/.tau/extensions/ (project), ~/.tau/extensions/ (user), and tau --extension/-e PATH. There is no agent/ root.
4 Wrong module shape Tau expects one level deep: *.py files, or a subdirectory containing extension.py, or a package declaring [tool.tau] extensions = [...]. A loose .ts file in a non-root directory fails all three.

The startup timings confirm it: capability:extension-modules:native: 5.4ms fired, found nothing in the real roots, and moved on. The file you wrote is inert.

The corrected extension

Python. Registers tools and a command — not a provider, because providers are not registerable. Place it at ~/.tau/extensions/vansrouter.py.

```python
"""VansRouter extension for Tau (omp).

Targets Tau >= 18.2.x, Phase 21 extension API.
Depends on: ExtensionAPI.register_tool, register_command, on(event).
Does NOT use provider registration -- that is a Phase 21 non-goal.

Install: copy to ~/.tau/extensions/vansrouter.py
Verify:  tau -e ~/.tau/extensions/vansrouter.py
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

from tau_agent.messages import TextContent
from tau_agent.tools import AgentTool, AgentToolResult
from tau_coding.extensions import ExtensionAPI


def _base() -> str:
    return (
        os.environ.get("VANSROUTER_URL")
        or os.environ.get("NINEROUTER_URL")
        or "http://127.0.0.1:20128"
    ).rstrip("/")


def _key() -> str:
    return (
        os.environ.get("VANSROUTER_API_KEY")
        or os.environ.get("NINEROUTER_KEY")
        or ""
    )


def _get(path: str, timeout: float = 5.0):
    req = urllib.request.Request(_base() + path)
    if key := _key():
        req.add_header("Authorization", f"Bearer {key}")
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as r:
        return json.loads(r.read().decode("utf-8"))


def _vansrouter_status() -> str:
    try:
        health = _get("/api/health", timeout=2.0)
    except Exception:
        health = None

    try:
        models = _get("/v1/models")
        count = len(models.get("data", []))
    except Exception as e:
        return f"VansRouter unreachable at {_base()}: {e}"

    key_state = "present" if _key() else "MISSING"
    return (
        f"base:   {_base()}\n"
        f"key:    {key_state}\n"
        f"health: {health}\n"
        f"models: {count}"
    )


def _vansrouter_models() -> str:
    try:
        data = _get("/v1/models")
    except Exception as e:
        return f"VansRouter unreachable: {e}"
    ids = [m.get("id", "?") for m in data.get("data", [])]
    return "\n".join(ids) if ids else "(no models)"


def setup(tau: ExtensionAPI) -> None:
    """Register VansRouter tools and command."""

    tau.register_tool(
        AgentTool(
            name="vansrouter_status",
            label="vansrouter_status",
            description=(
                "Report VansRouter reachability, API key presence, "
                "and discovered model count."
            ),
            parameters={"type": "object", "properties": {}, "required": []},
            execute=lambda args: AgentToolResult(
                content=[TextContent(text=_vansrouter_status())]
            ),
        )
    )

    tau.register_tool(
        AgentTool(
            name="vansrouter_models",
            label="vansrouter_models",
            description=(
                "List model IDs currently exposed by the local VansRouter "
                "instance at /v1/models."
            ),
            parameters={"type": "object", "properties": {}, "required": []},
            execute=lambda args: AgentToolResult(
                content=[TextContent(text=_vansrouter_models())]
            ),
        )
    )

    def _cmd(args: str, ctx) -> None:
        sub = (args or "").strip().split() or ["status"]
        if sub[0] == "models":
            ctx.send_user_message(_vansrouter_models())
        elif sub[0] == "cache":
            ctx.send_user_message(
                "VansRouter caching is server-side; no client cache in this extension."
            )
        else:
            ctx.send_user_message(_vansrouter_status())

    tau.register_command(
        name="vansrouter",
        description="VansRouter status | models | cache",
        handler=_cmd,
    )

    @tau.on("session_start")
    def _on_start(_event, ctx) -> None:
        state = _vansrouter_status().splitlines()[0]
        ctx.send_user_message(f"[vansrouter] {state}")
```

Install

```bash
# 1. Create the real discovery root (not agent/)
mkdir -p ~/.tau/extensions

# 2. Remove the broken file from the non-root
rm -f ~/.tau/agent/extensions/vansrouter.ts
rmdir ~/.tau/agent/extensions 2>/dev/null || true

# 3. Write the Python file there
#    (paste the block above, or use the write tool)

# 4. Verify discovery without starting a session
tau -e ~/.tau/extensions/vansrouter.py --version

# 5. Confirm the tools are visible
tau --list-tools 2>/dev/null | grep vansrouter
```

First observable signal of success

Run tau and type /vansrouter at the prompt. If you see base: http://127.0.0.1:20128 and key: present, the extension loaded. If you see nothing, the discovery root is still wrong.

Why this is the correct shape

Provider registration was the wrong target from the start. Tau's Phase 21 non-goal list includes it by name.
